sections.context: The staged Astro repository already has a deliberately small preview slice and a green npm quality contract. The next safe move is to prove that slice in a representative route, exercise the editorial ownership boundary, and collect preview evidence before any production integration. This plan must remain planning-only: no product implementation, deployment activation, credentials, DNS, R2 bindings, or cutover changes.
sections.approach: Execute three ordered, independently reviewable preview tasks. First validate the representative route and its intentional 404 behavior. Then exercise the existing non-secret Tina fixture/content contract while preserving senshac-content as the editorial system of record. Finally run the complete quality, secret-boundary, accessibility/SEO placeholder, and production-exclusion checks and attach evidence. Keep implementation changes out of this run; any discovered defect becomes a follow-up seed rather than an opportunistic product change.

alternatives.rejected_because: The cutover specification requires a non-production preview and explicit acceptance evidence before production boundaries or credentials are configured.

alternatives.rejected_because: Separate route, content-boundary, and quality evidence gives the next preview work narrow ownership and preserves ordered plan-run execution.

sections.context: The sitewide audit found that Tina already supports safe rich text for selected long-form fields, but the font pairing is currently hard-coded and plain string controls are not appropriate for arbitrary rich-text editing. The user approved bounded editorial control. The current Sinteca-body/Jozsika-display appearance must remain the default, while editors need a small, understandable Tina control to select approved sitewide typography pairings.
sections.approach: Add one Site Configuration enum with three reviewed pairings mapped to existing local fonts: current Senshac (Sinteca body/Jozsika display), Sinteca throughout, and Editorial (Jozsika body/Sinteca display). Keep font sizes, weights, colors, layout, labels, and action/accessibility fields constrained. Make Astro backward-compatible with old content that omits the setting, apply the font roles through shared CSS variables across both layouts, and test the Tina schema and rendered browser behavior. Update senshac-content's config/schema/tests in its separate claimed Seed; web support must land before any future content publication.

steps.title: Add the Tina typography preset contract and backward-compatible runtime default
Apply typography tokens sitewide and verify editor and browser behavior

risks: Old content revisions may omit the field; the runtime must default to the existing Senshac pairing.
Some font assets support only selected weights; preset mapping must use existing, verified font assets and preserve CSS-owned weights.
Legacy layout styles or direct font-family declarations may bypass shared CSS variables; audit and contract-test both layouts.
Content repository changes can trigger an automated web build after merge; keep the content PR unmerged until web support lands and deployment is separately authorized.
Tina schema changes require a generated tina-lock.json from the actual Tina dev command, not manual edits or test discovery.
acceptance: Tina Site Configuration exposes exactly three labeled, documented typography presets and persists the selected enum.
The current Senshac pairing remains the default in content and in the runtime when older content omits the setting.
Only allowlisted font pairs are rendered; no user-provided CSS or font values reach style output.
Shared body/display font roles update across localized and legacy layouts while the wordmark remains fixed.
Long-form rich-text controls remain safe and semantic; operational, form, action, and accessibility copy remains constrained.
Content and web quality gates pass; Tina lock is regenerated; desktop/mobile browser contracts verify the default and alternate roles on fresh output.
Seeds Doctor passes in both focused repositories, and no PR is merged or deployed without explicit approval.
